notes: Small grass forms: mounds, verges, tufts. gradientBase/gradientHeight are OBJECT space and this geometry is unit-sized: metre-scale values here saturate the sweep to a constant and switch the vertical gradient off entirely, which is how every instanced asset in the greybox lost it. Saturation corrected: lit must sit BELOW shadow in chroma (measured -0.15 across references); the earlier ART_BIBLE rule had this inverted. Brush overlay reduced 1.45 -> 0.0: the painterly direction is abandoned (ART_BIBLE 1) and this was still running at full strength, which is the camouflage mottle on terrain. PAINTERLY OVERLAY REMOVED IN THE DATA, all five knobs, not just the obvious one. `brushStrength` was already 0 on this def and the surface still rendered as leopard print, because `brushHue` (an albedo hue rotation), `detailStrength` (a normal perturbation), `regionStep` (a coarse mass mask) and `reliefShade` (an AMBIENT mottle) are all read independently of it in painterly.ts. Measured on one flat rock facet, a 20x20 window ran luma sd 0.106-0.148 against 0.015-0.042 for a facet in refs/genshin/grasslands.jpg — 3.5-10x. The whole point of a plane-cut solid is that a facet is exactly planar so the 3-stop ramp reads it as ONE flat value, and this was destroying that on every asset in the library. ART_BIBLE 1: "No brush-stroke overlay on terrain. Surfaces are clean." HUE CORRECTED OFF CHARTREUSE. The lit stop was #cbe86b at hue 70 and the top #d8ff7a at hue 73; sampled off refs/genshin/grasslands.jpg the lit grass is #85CD4A / #8CDD57 at hue 93-96, saturation 0.61-0.64. Hue 70 is the acid-yellow-green cast ART_BIBLE 1 rejects by name, and a tuft instanced tens of thousands of times is the largest single contributor to it. The shadow stop also moves off the near-black #2b7a29 toward the reference's grass shade, which is still unmistakably GREEN at hue 133.
